First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{q}^{2}+2 & =0 \\ 6{q}^{2} & =-2 \\ {q}^{2} & =-\frac{2}{6} \\ {q}^{2} & =-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

By taking square root, we obtain:

$$
q=\pm \sqrt{-\frac{1}{3}}
$$

We now rewrite $q$ using the imaginary unit $\text{i}=\sqrt{-1}\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =\pm \sqrt{-\frac{1}{3}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-1)} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{3}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{1}}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\text{i} \\  & =\pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
